statusText: Watch: Tail eases to 20% after NQ retraced roughly 112 points off a marginal new overnight low at 30,373.00.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail at 20% sits at the lower edge of the watch band and below the block threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window runs 13:30Z to 15:00Z, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures retrace about 112 points off a marginal 30,373.00 overnight low; Tail eases to 20% with Stress at 78%
body: The 06:00Z clock-hour produced the first genuine retracement of the overnight decline. NQ December reads 30,485.50 at 06:16:27Z on Yahoo Finance, -80.75 and -0.26% against a 30,566.25 previous close, with a Globex range of 30,373.00 to 30,616.00; Investing.com independently shows 30,486.00 on a 02:16 ET print with a 30,372.25 low. The overnight low therefore extended about 36 points below the 30,409.25 level that held through the previous two hours, and price then recovered roughly 112 points from it. That is the opposite of a failed retracement: the break was rejected rather than continued, and the session loss narrowed from -0.45% an hour ago to -0.26%. Monday's cash session remains the more informative structural reference. The Nasdaq-100 index closed at 30,276.81, -1.08%, having traded a low of 30,081.06 and a high of 30,480.40, so roughly 195 points of retracement developed into the close. Mean reversion has been working on both the daily and the overnight timeframe. The difficult environment is unchanged and is where the weight sits. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.25% after touching 5.27% on Monday, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year reached about 5.55%, the highest since 2004, with positioning shifting toward further Fed tightening. WTI trades near $93.95, up about 1.45%, with Brent firm, as the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz remains unresolved. Monday's decline was led by semiconductors, with Arm down about 9%, Qualcomm about 6% and Marvell about 5% while the semiconductor ETF fell 3% against a 1.3% decline in the Nasdaq-100 ETF, and OpenAI's pause of next-generation model training weighed separately on the AI trade. Against that, the Asian session closed mixed rather than uniformly risk-off: the Nikkei fell 1.2% to 65,114.64, the Kospi 0.6% to 6,847.56 and the Hang Seng 0.5% to 24,516.46, while the Shanghai Composite added 0.1% and the S&P/ASX 200 added 0.1%. The 10-year yield paused its runup overnight. VIX closed at 16.07, up 8.1% but low in absolute terms. No repeated extension after a failed retracement has been observed. Tail therefore eases three points to 20% and the dominant mode moves from trend-down to mixed, because the aligned amplifiers remain real but are being expressed as a difficult, high-volatility environment rather than as a pathological price path. Stress at 78% carries that weight. Confidence holds at 88% on two independent agreeing futures feeds timestamped within the current clock-hour, verified Asian cash closes, verified yield and oil levels and a verified seven-day calendar. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of the run, was about 5.3 hours old with collectionStatus partial, and was therefore treated as stale and not used as material evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from the European morning of 28 September to the hour before this assessment, and every one of the 24 slots has a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 24% Tail with Stress at 80% and stayed inside a 17-27% Tail range throughout. Two hours reached the elevated band and neither persisted: 09:00Z at 26% during European long-end repricing and 14:00Z at 27% around the US cash open, both back inside the watch band within one hour. Tail fell to 17-19% across the late US session and the first overnight hours as Monday's cash market closed having retraced roughly 195 points off its low. The last five hours firmed back to 20-24% as the Asian session traded lower and the overnight low was probed, with the dominant mode alternating between trend-down and mixed. Stress stayed persistently high, between 76% and 85%, reflecting record long-end yields and high oil rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Confidence improved steadily from 82% to 88% as live evidence accumulated.
outlookSummary: The conditional path opens at 20% for the current 06:00Z hour, where the observed 112-point retracement off the 30,373.00 low is the evidence carrying the judgment. It holds at 20-21% through late Asian trade and the European cash open, then marks 09:00Z at 23% because that is the recurring long-end repricing window which reached 26% on Monday. It eases to 21-22% across the quiet pre-US hours and firms to 23% into the 13:00Z Case-Shiller release and the 13:30Z cash open. The single elevated stretch is 14:00Z to 15:00Z at 26% and 25%, covering the JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases landing 30 minutes into the cash session; the dominant mode is marked event/whipsaw there and the danger window closes at 15:00Z. The path then decays through the afternoon, crosses back below the watch threshold at 21:00Z once the cash market closes, and bottoms at 17% overnight. It firms again from 02:00Z on 30 September, reaching 22% by the European morning as positioning begins for the ADP, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP block. Confidence decays from 88% to 79% across the projection as distance from the live evidence anchor grows. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
